title: Stop My Dancing! Understanding, Detecting and Attributing Motion-Aware Deepfake Videos
title_zh: Stop My Dancing!理解、检测和归因运动感知Deepfake视频

paragraphs.en: 本文提出了一种名为MoDA的新防御框架，专门用于检测和归因运动感知Deepfake视频，显著提高了检测和属性识别的准确性。 Pose-guided diffusion models can now synthesize entire human figures in motion, spawning a new class of deepfakes: Motion Aware Deepfake (MAD) that have already reached hundreds of millions of viewers. To better understand this emerging threat, we construct the first MAD-specific benchmark and measurement framework, containing over 1.5 million frames that mix 1,363 real and 30,122 synthetic videos from six controllable generators, with realistic perturbations and open-world evaluation splits. Then, we dissect MAD and discover that, despite their global coherence, these videos betray faint yet reliable cues: because the model relies on limited input frames for motion synthesis, it must predict and simulate coherent movement at motion boundaries, thereby producing high-frequency artifacts along with model-specific spectral fingerprints. Based on the observations obtained from analysis on dataset, we propose MoDA, the first defense framework tailored to detect and attribute MAD videos. MoDA couples spatial semantics with steganalysis-rich frequency features via cross-domain alignment and multi-scale aggregation, achieving 94.8% in-distribution and 89.1% cross-dataset detection accuracy gains of 10% to 25% over prior work and 91.5% model attribution accuracy. MoDA achieves 81.94% accuracy on 200 clips produced by two unseen commercial MAD platforms, indicating promising zero-shot transfer, and 78.13% detection accuracy on 1,200 unseen MAD video clips (55k frames in total) collected from the open Internet. Under white-box, gray-box, and black-box adaptive attacks, MoDA maintains relatively stable detection and attribution performance while the accuracies of the baselines drop rapidly.
paragraphs.zh: 本文提出了一种名为MoDA的新防御框架，专门用于检测和归因运动感知Deepfake视频，显著提高了检测和属性识别的准确性。基于姿态引导的扩散模型现在能够合成完整的动态人体形象，由此催生了一类新的Deepfake：运动感知Deepfake（MAD），其观看量已达到数亿次。 为了更好地理解这一新兴威胁，我们构建了首个针对MAD的基准测试和测量框架，其中包含超过150万帧画面，混合了来自六个可控生成器的1,363个真实视频和30,122个合成视频，并加入了逼真的扰动以及开放世界的评估划分。 接着，我们对MAD进行了深入分析，发现尽管这些视频在整体上具有连贯性，但它们仍暴露出微弱但可靠的线索：由于模型依赖有限的输入帧进行运动合成，因此必须在运动边界处预测并模拟连贯的运动，从而产生高频伪影以及模型特有的频谱指纹。 基于对数据集分析所得的观察结果，我们提出了MoDA——首个专为检测和归因MAD视频而设计的防御框架。 MoDA通过跨域对齐和多尺度聚合，将空间语义与富含隐写分析信息的频率特征相结合，在分布内检测中实现了94.8%的准确率，在跨数据集检测中较以往工作提升了10%至25%，模型归因准确率达到91.5%。 MoDA在由两个未见的商业MAD平台生成的200个片段上达到了81.94%的准确率，显示出良好的零样本迁移能力；在从开放互联网收集的1,200个未见MAD视频片段（共5.5万帧）上，其检测准确率为78.13%。 在白盒、灰盒和黑盒自适应攻击下，MoDA保持了相对稳定的检测和归因性能，而基线方法的准确率则迅速下降。
